payload.task: self_diffusion of Cu in perfect fcc Cu at 300 K by MD (cm2/s)
payload.reason: Premise check failed: the quantity cannot be measured with MD as posed. (1) In a perfect (defect-free) fcc crystal there is no diffusion mechanism to sample: lattice self-diffusion in Cu goes through vacancies, and a perfect crystal has none. Over any MD-accessible time, atoms only vibrate around their lattice sites, so the MSD levels off at the thermal vibration amplitude (<u^2> ~ 0.01-0.02 A^2 at 300 K). Fitting a slope to that plateau gives zero plus noise. That would be a fake number, not a diffusion coefficient. (2) The real physical value is far too small to resolve. Using approximate Arrhenius parameters for tracer self-diffusion in Cu (activation energy Q ~ 2.0-2.2 eV, prefactor D0 ~ 0.1-1 cm2/s), D(300 K) = D0 exp(-Q/kT) ~ 1e-38 to 1e-34 cm2/s. The kT = 0.02585 eV puts the exponent near -80. Even a long 10 ns run with an MSD resolution of ~0.01 A^2 can only detect D down to about 1e-11 cm2/s. That is roughly 23 or more orders of magnitude above the true value. (3) Adding a vacancy does not fix this. The equilibrium vacancy fraction at 300 K is ~exp(-E_f/kT) with E_f ~ 1.2-1.3 eV, so about 1e-21 to 1e-20. Any vacancy in an MD cell of 1e3-1e6 atoms would be far out of equilibrium. Even then, the vacancy hop rate (migration barrier ~0.7 eV) is ~1e1-1e2 per second, so no hop would be seen in nanoseconds. Validation is not possible either: no independent known result can be recovered with this setup, because no direct MD protocol for this observable at 300 K has a nonzero signal. So I am not posting a value. Reporting 0 or a noise-level upper bound as 'self_diffusion' would be misleading.

details.estimated_physical_D_300K_cm2_s: ~1e-38 to 1e-34. This is an order-of-magnitude Arrhenius extrapolation from approximate literature parameters. It is not a computed result.
proposed_well_posed_alternatives: A: Vacancy-mediated D(T) = f a^2 nu* exp(-(E_f+E_m)/kT) with correlation factor f=0.781 for fcc. Compute vacancy formation energy E_f with a relaxed supercell and migration energy E_m with NEB, using the same potential (EAM Cu or a MACE-type MLIP). Get the attempt frequency from harmonic TST. Validate E_f, E_m and Q against measured values (Q ~ 2.0-2.1 eV), then extrapolate to 300 K with the uncertainty propagated from Q.

B: Direct MD of vacancy-containing Cu at high temperature (~1000-1300 K, below the 1357.77 K melting point). Measure D = c_v * D_vac. Validate the Arrhenius fit against measured high-temperature tracer data, then extrapolate. A 300 K extrapolation is uncertain by several orders of magnitude.

C: Liquid Cu self-diffusion just above melting. This is directly measurable by MD in 100 ps-1 ns with an Einstein MSD fit plus finite-size (Yeh-Hummer) correction, and it gives a validation target of order 1e-5 cm2/s.
details.mechanism_note: Self-diffusion in fcc Cu is vacancy-mediated. A perfect crystal has zero diffusive pathways on MD timescales.
